subject: Linguistics
title: Infixes
description: A fast breakdown of Infixes for builders.

hook.text: In Tagalog 'sulat' means writing, but 'sumulat' means 'wrote'—notice the '-um-' inside.

buildup.text: An infix is a morpheme inserted into the middle of a word—rare in English, common elsewhere.

discovery.text: English's closest infixes are expletives inserted for emphasis: 'abso-bloody-lutely.'

twist.text: Even informal infixing follows rules—you insert at a specific syllable boundary, not randomly.

climax.text: Infixes prove that morphological operations can target any position in a word.

punchline.text: Some morphemes live in the middle of the action.

quiz.question: Where does an infix appear?
options: Inside the root of a word
